newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tryg-Baltica sees better combined ratio.
newsitem.headline: Tryg-Baltica sees better combined ratio.

text.p: Danish insurer Tryg-Baltica said on Monday it expected its combined ratio to continue to improve in 1997, setting a target of 103 percent for 1998.

"The improvement in the combined ratio is expected to go on in 1997 due to already implemented rises in car insurance premiums, increased focus on client profitability and higher quality servicing of accident insurance," Tryg-Baltica, Denmark's biggest insurer, said in its 1996 report.
The Tryg-Baltica combined ratio was 107.1 percent in 1996, against 109.7 in the previous year and the group said it set a target for 103 percent for 1998.
The result was markedly better than Tryg-Baltica's forecast last August of a net profit in the 550-600 million range for the full year.

Net profit at 1.068 billion crowns was only slightly up on 1995's full year 1.060 billion crowns but Tryg-Baltica's board expressed satisfaction with the result which was the first for a whole financial year since the May 1995 merger of former Baltica Forsikring and Tryg Forsikring.

It said that the result corresponded to a 16.8 percent return on average equity of 6.814 billion crowns after provision for dividends and exceeded statutory Danish solvency requirements by almost four billion crowns.

Tryg-Baltica said total insurance premium income increased by 14.5 percent to 9.309 billion crowns in 1996, with non-life earned premiums rising 4.8 percent and regular life insurance business up by the same percentage over 1995.
It said investment income had been favourably influenced by developments in financial markets and put 1996's gross expense ratio at 25.9 percent. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
